blocks.etymology: The verb is from Middle English tasten, borrowed from Old French taster (“to taste, touch or hit”), from unattested Vulgar Latin *tastāre (“to touch or feel”), from *taxitāre, an innovated iterative form of Classical Latin taxāre (“to touch sharply”), from tangere (“to touch, to grasp”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *teh₂g-, which is assumed to have had the same meaning as tangere. The noun came from the verb, and the two conflated after English lost its infinitive suffix -en, though tasten was most likely already used nominatively (as a gerund), similar to Modern English tasting.

senses.definition: To produce a particular sensation of flavor when someone puts it in their mouth.

examples.en: This fresh juice tastes like ripe mangoes.
examples.vi: Món nước ép tươi này có vị như xoài chín.

senses.definition: To put a small bite or sip of food or drink into your mouth to check its flavor.

examples.en: Please taste the broth before serving it.
examples.vi: Xin hãy nếm nước dùng trước khi múc ra phục vụ.

senses.definition: To detect or distinguish a particular flavor while eating or drinking.

examples.en: Can you taste the ginger in this tea?
examples.vi: Bạn có nếm thấy vị gừng trong tách trà này không?

senses.definition: To experience something personally for a short period of time.

examples.en: After years of hard training, they finally tasted victory.
examples.vi: Sau nhiều năm khổ luyện, cuối cùng họ cũng nếm mùi chiến thắng.
